author: imani_fairley
subject: Farmers market opens Saturday at Osprey Commons
body: The Tallgrass Ridge Farmers Market is back at Osprey Commons this Saturday from 8 to noon, with 23 vendors on the lower lot and a new seedling table by the gazebo. The north lot is closed for the water main work, so park on Pilcher Lane and walk in. The honey stand is still cash only, so come prepared. We need four more volunteers for the 10 a.m. ticket table, just reply if you can help.

comments.author: sunita_malhotra
comments.body: I'm bringing a few flats of basil and sweet peppers for the seedling table, so the gardeners will have something to take home. Come before nine if you want the early pick.

comments.author: greta_oseland
comments.body: Perfect, I'll bring my wagon for the haul. Is the honey stand back this year? I missed it last fall.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Pilcher Lane is a nightmare by nine, the minivan line starts at the stop sign. Go early or walk over from the library lot, it's about ten minutes.

comments.author: vivian_oduya
comments.body: Thank you for organizing this, Imani. Are dogs allowed on the lower lot, or should I leave mine at home?

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: Dogs on leash are fine under the park rules, and the lower lot is grass, so bring a bag. I'll post the full vendor list on the gardeners board Friday night.

author: bernadette_hughes
subject: Friends of the Fennimore Branch book sale, this weekend
body: The Friends group is holding its fall book sale in the Fennimore Branch community room, with paperbacks at a quarter and hardcovers at a dollar. Donations of gently used books can go in the side door until the Thursday before the sale. Cookbooks and children's picture books always go first, so come early on the Friday preview. Members get in an hour early, and membership is five dollars at the desk.

comments.author: frances_hollis
comments.body: I'll be there Friday with my book club bag. Do you need volunteers for the cash box? I can do a two-hour shift.

comments.author: bernadette_hughes
comments.body: Yes please, the Saturday cash box needs two people. Find me at the front desk at nine and we'll get you set up.

comments.author: greta_oseland
comments.body: Penrose Lane Books runs a swap shelf by the register if you want to trade before the sale, which saves a trip.

comments.author: odessa_wright
comments.body: The cookbooks are gone within twenty minutes on preview day, I learned that the hard way. Bring a tote bag and a strong elbow for the crowd.

author: walt_gerrity
subject: Greaves Mill Harvest Festival is this Sunday at the old pavilion
body: The Harvest Festival is Sunday from noon to six at the Greaves Mill pavilion, with a hayride from the old mill gate and free apple cider from the church women's group. Kids can enter the pumpkin contest at the picnic table until 2 p.m. The Oriole Diner is bringing its pie table back, which is the real reason I'm writing. Bring a lawn chair, because the grass by the creek stays wet until noon.

comments.author: anton_pelc
comments.body: Does the hayride stop at the trail head by the culvert? I can ride over from the Ilsted end if it does.

comments.author: walt_gerrity
comments.body: It does, Anton, the wagon turns around at the culvert every half hour. Ask at the cider table about the pie list, it sells out before three.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: Parking on Mill Road is going to be a mess again, so walk over from the Corran Avenue lot. Grumbling aside, the cider is worth the walk.

comments.author: lena_hoffer
comments.body: Hi, I'm new in town and don't have a car yet. Is there a bus that goes out to the pavilion on Sunday?

author: raj_pandey
subject: Food shelf 5K on Saturday at Vantage Creek, registration still open
body: The Ridgeline Food Shelf 5K starts at 8 a.m. Saturday at the Vantage Creek trailhead, with a loop along the creek and a kids' fun run at 9. Entry is 25 dollars, or bring two cans of soup to the packet table and it drops to 15. The course is crushed limestone with one hill at mile two that everyone complains about. I'm volunteering at the water stop, so find me if you want to pace together.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Good luck to everyone running. Please keep the kids off the road at the creek crossing, the county says the bridge gets narrow near the water stop.

comments.author: gabriel_nunez
comments.body: Hollis Brick Oven is donating pizza for the finish line tent, so come see me after. Mention the 5K and I'll add extra pepperoni.

comments.author: wade_tanaka
comments.body: Park at the Knoll lot and walk over, because the gravel trailhead fills by 7:30 every year. Learned that one the hard way.

comments.author: raj_pandey
comments.body: Thanks Wade, I'll post a shuttle note in the group this week. Curtis, thanks for the creek reminder too.

comments.author: imani_fairley
comments.body: Signing up my whole block! Tagging Lupe and Colleen so we can make a team.

author: beverly_tuttle
subject: First Hollow Methodist fall supper, sign-up sheet in the narthex
body: First Hollow Methodist is hosting its fall church supper Thursday from 5 to 7:30 in the fellowship hall. We're serving chicken and noodles, green beans, and the apple crisp the women's circle is known for. The suggested donation is 8 dollars a plate, and kids under ten eat free. We still need people for desserts and clean-up, so please sign the sheet by the coat rack or message me. The rolls are from Marrow & Yeast again this year.

comments.author: noel_brandvold
comments.body: Hi, I'm new in town and I'd love to come. Is the supper open to people who aren't members of the church?

comments.author: beverly_tuttle
comments.body: Absolutely, everyone is welcome, just come hungry. Ask for me at the door and I'll walk you to a seat.

comments.author: vivian_oduya
comments.body: Thank you for organizing this, Mrs. Tuttle. I signed up for the dessert table.

comments.author: jonah_fitch
comments.body: I'll be there. Is the apple crisp made with regular flour, or do I need to bring something for my gluten-free kid?

comments.author: imani_fairley
comments.body: Ask Beverly at the door. The baked apples on the side are plain fruit, but the crisp is made with regular flour, so bring a dish if you need one.

comments.author: kofi_mensah
comments.body: Count me in for clean-up, I'll bring the van for the folding tables.

author: anton_pelc
subject: Vantage Creek cleanup this Saturday, gloves and bags provided
body: The Vantage Creek cleanup is this Saturday, meeting at the bridge on Auberon Road at 8 a.m. The county is supplying gloves, grabbers and orange bags, and the city picks up full bags on Monday. Last spring we pulled out nine tires and a shopping cart. We're also planting sedge along the bank, so bring boots, because the mud is bad past the second culvert.

comments.author: gunnar_sorensen
comments.body: I can bring the trailer and a chainsaw in case somebody needs a branch cut. I'm not promising I'll be friendly about it.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: Park on the shoulder by the bridge, not the grass. Somebody's car sank there last year.

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: Our parents group can bring snacks for the volunteers, and my kids want to hunt for turtles.

comments.author: eli_stroud
comments.body: Last time we found a shopping cart and my boys named it Gerald. Please bring a wagon for Gerald's return.

comments.author: anton_pelc
comments.body: Thanks Maribel. The grabbers in the blue bin are kid-sized, and snacks go by the bridge at 8:30.

author: sunita_malhotra
subject: Fall plant swap in the back lot, bring your divisions
body: Saturday morning plant swap in the back lot of Hatch and Hyacinth, 9 to 11, for anyone with divisions to share. Bring hostas, daylilies, mint, or whatever you've been thinning out. We'll have a table for seed packets and a bin of clean pots, and I'll have the coffee going. Please label your plants, I'm tired of guessing what the orange ones are.

comments.author: ruth_ellery
comments.body: I'll bring the bearded iris divisions, they need thinning badly. Is the swap open to people who only have seeds?

comments.author: sunita_malhotra
comments.body: Seeds are welcome, we have a seed table by the side door. Please bring labels too, Ruth.

comments.author: deb_halvorsen
comments.body: There's no shade on the back lot until the sun clears the garage, so bring a hat and some water.

comments.author: june_akers
comments.body: My daughter wants to trade her sunflower seeds for basil. Can kids trade too, or do the grown-ups have to do it?

comments.author: gil_fenner
comments.body: I'll bring a wheelbarrow to haul the pots back. Pruett Hardware donated the bin of four-inch pots, so grab what you need.

comments.author: lupe_ochoa
comments.body: Adding this to the group calendar and telling the book club. Tern and Thistle said they'd keep a sign-up sheet at the counter for anyone who wants to bring a plant.

author: owen_pruitt
subject: Bus 14 is moving its stop on Dunmore Court, starting Monday
body: Heads up for Millrace families: the district moved Bus 14's pickup from the Dunmore Court corner to the cul-de-sac behind the community center, starting Monday. The new time is 7:12 instead of 7:05, which means my youngest is going to miss the breakfast rush. The letter says it's about the road work on Velder, and it doesn't say when that ends.

comments.author: jonah_fitch
comments.body: Reading the letter twice, the new cul-de-sac is about a mile from my son's stop, so I'm glad I'm not the only one confused. Did the district say whether the time change is permanent?

comments.author: mateo_gallegos
comments.body: I can drive the kids to the community center on Monday if anyone needs it. Text me before seven and I'll be there.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Permanent until the road work is done, per the letter, and they say spring. Ask the transportation office for the route map, it shows the new stop.

comments.author: dorothy_breen
comments.body: Hello all, I'm new and sorry to ask, but is Bus 14 the one that goes to the middle school?

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Yes, it's the Pembrook bus. Don't apologize, everybody asks in the first month.

author: colleen_brandt
subject: Ridgeline Elementary PTA pizza and wreath night this Friday
body: Ridgeline Elementary PTA is doing pizza night this Friday in the cafeteria, 5 to 7:30, with two slices and a drink for six dollars. The wreath pre-orders close Sunday, and the fifth grade band needs the money for new music stands. The pizza comes from Hollis Brick Oven, so the crust is great, and we take cash or card at the table. Thanks, everyone, and we need more hands on the drink table!

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: Our family is in for three pizzas. I'll pick up the wreath orders from the front office Monday if anyone wants them delivered to Tamarack.

comments.author: sadie_kimbrough
comments.body: New to town and I have no idea what the PTA does, but pizza sounds like the right way to meet people! Do you need help on the drink table?

comments.author: colleen_brandt
comments.body: Yes, Sadie! Message me and I'll put you on the table. Welcome to town, we're so glad you're here.

comments.author: hal_brenneman
comments.body: Put me down for two wreaths. The last fundraiser bought the new bleachers, so I can sit on them and complain about the price.

comments.author: corinne_avila
comments.body: The wreath order form has a QR code on the back, which is faster than the paper one. Also ask Hollis for extra cheese on the first slice, it's worth it.

author: sadie_kimbrough
subject: What do you all do for teacher appreciation week at Ridgeline?
body: Hi all, we moved in three weeks ago and my daughter just started third grade at Ridgeline Elementary. Teacher appreciation week is coming up, and I have no idea what the other families usually do. Is there a sign-up for a class gift, or should I just bring something to the front office? Any advice on a budget would be wonderful, thank you!

comments.author: june_akers
comments.body: I'm a teacher's aide, and the gift that always lands is a card with a handwritten note from each kid. Skip the mugs, they end up with forty.

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: Our parents group runs a sign-up for the class gift each spring, so I'll message you the link tonight.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: Welcome to the neighborhood, Sadie. Bring a box of donuts from Marrow & Yeast to the front office on Friday, because the staff eats them fast.

comments.author: sadie_kimbrough
comments.body: Thank you June, the handwritten card idea is perfect, and I'll ask the other moms about the link.

comments.author: vivian_oduya
comments.body: At my last school the front office wanted a fruit tray rather than gifts, which was easy to split. Keep it simple and it will go a long way.

author: maribel_serrano
subject: Fall youth soccer sign-ups close Friday, ages 5 to 12
body: Tallgrass Ridge Youth Soccer is taking fall sign-ups through Friday at the Vantage Creek fields, for ages 5 to 12. Fees are 85 dollars, with a scholarship form available from any coach, and practices start the 24th. We still need two coaches for the U10 girls and a field marshal for Saturdays, so ping me if you can help. Sign up through the parents circle page, because the old form is closed. Juniper Row Landscaping paid for the new jerseys, so thank them if you see them.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: My kids are in, and I'll volunteer for carpool. Hopefully the Saturday games won't clash with the bus schedule again.

comments.author: eli_stroud
comments.body: Is there a coach needed for U6? I can help on the sideline, I'm bad at drills but good at high fives.

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: Yes, U6 has two open spots. Email me directly and I'll send the coach packet.

comments.author: samir_qureshi
comments.body: Our family needs the scholarship form. Do we pick it up from a coach on the field, or is there a copy online?

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: Coaches have paper copies at the Saturday field, or I can send the PDF. The form is due with the fee, so bring both.

author: corinne_avila
subject: Only one crossing guard for three crosswalks at Ridgeline
body: I counted this morning, and Ridgeline Elementary has one crossing guard covering the Ostler Road crossing, the Pell Bend crosswalk, and the back gate on Thackery. Two kids I walk every day almost got clipped by a truck making the turn. The district says it's posting the job, but the pay matches the lunch aide and nobody has applied in two months. Has anyone heard whether the city will pay for a second guard?

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Call the board and describe it as a traffic hazard, not a wish list. They respond to bus-speed problems faster than anything else.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Volunteer firefighter here. Report each near miss to the non-emergency line with the time and plate if you got one, because it creates a record.

comments.author: lupe_ochoa
comments.body: I'll share this on the parents thread and ask the PTA about a petition. Corinne, could you post the times you counted?

comments.author: corinne_avila
comments.body: Yes, I'll post the counts. Monday from 7:35 to 8:05, three crosswalks, one guard, and forty-one kids crossing without an adult.

comments.author: jolene_harkins
comments.body: I heard the city has a crosswalk study on the agenda. Ask Wendell Pike, he reads every agenda and will know the date.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Fine. The district just handed out new sweatshirts for the fall grab bag. Priorities, apparently.
